learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparing numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected about ten times sooner and locked the prediction for accelerating the already fast second step of A to B to C.
observations.exploration: Enabled step 2 times ten: half-time changed from 7.03 s to 6.94 s. Enabled step 1 too: both times ten gave 0.70 s. Selected only step 1 times ten: half-time 0.80 s. The comparison history retained all four conditions.
observations.reveal: The reveal corrected the answer to almost no sooner and accurately compared 7.03, 6.94 and 0.80 s. It explained the narrowest gate as the rate-determining step and said that is the step to target for speeding the reaction.
observations.visual: Inspected the inline dark 1257 by 936 screenshot after accelerating step 2. A two-gate diagram appeared over a product-versus-time graph; the original dashed and new pink curves almost overlapped near the half-product line, with 7.03 and 6.94 s labels.
observations.isolation: No-history evaluation preview banner present. Visible trust count ignored.
observations.reference: Own CUA tab 543884163 snapshots and inspected inline screenshot; no screenshot file saved.

prediction.reason: The question targets a whole-process versus component-speed misconception.
prediction.evidence: Selected tenfold improvement despite the first step remaining slow.

interaction.reason: Independent toggles and an isolated bottleneck case identify which improvement matters.
interaction.evidence: Fast step alone barely changed half-time; slow step alone nearly matched accelerating both.

payoff.reason: The reveal connects observed contrasts to a rate-limiting mechanism.
payoff.evidence: It accurately compares fast-only and slow-only results.

clarity.reason: Persistent curve comparisons and explicit half-times make the tiny versus large effects readable.
clarity.evidence: The fast-only curve nearly overlaps the baseline while labels quantify the difference.

transfer.reason: The bottleneck principle is generalized but no new reaction or external application is developed.
transfer.evidence: The ending remains within the same two-step chain.

accessibility.evidence: Keyboard, focus, contrast audit, phone, zoom/reflow and motion unknown.

surprise.reason: A tenfold component improvement can barely affect the overall result.
surprise.evidence: The fast-step change reduced half-time by only 0.09 s.

visualExplanation.reason: The gate analogy and overlaid product curves connect mechanism to timing.
visualExplanation.evidence: Nearly overlapping baseline and fast-only curves support the null result.

playfulness.reason: Toggles support a compact factorial comparison.
playfulness.evidence: Fast-only, both and slow-only conditions can be selected.

practicalValue.reason: It clarifies where an improvement should be targeted.
practicalValue.evidence: The reveal identifies the rate-determining step.

depth.reason: The isolated slow-step condition separates the contribution of the two changes.
depth.evidence: Slow-only 0.80 s is close to both 0.70 s, unlike fast-only 6.94 s.

complexity.reason: The gate metaphor is familiar, while reaction chains and product half-time add technical interpretation.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Moderate: distinguish local rate changes from whole-chain throughput.
complexity.interfaceBurden: Low: two toggles and an isolation preset.
complexity.conceptualChallenge: Improving a nonbottleneck has little effect while the bottleneck remains.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: Reaction intermediates and rate-determining steps are introduced.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: Moderate: A to B to C notation, product curves and half-time values.

whyCool: The nearly useless improvement and the effective one can be isolated with the same tenfold speed change.
caveat: The toy fixes a two-step chain with a hundredfold initial rate difference; real mechanisms may have changing rate control.
missingEvidence: No fresh rate ratio or reaction chain was tested.
